messages:
tina ng: Hi all, first week here! Running into a weird postgres init issue on macOS (Apple Silicon, Ventura) when using a host bind mount for ./pgdata. Container exits with initdb permission denied. Anyone have a clean, repeatable workaround? :grimacing:

Tina: Logs snippet:
```
postgres_1  | initdb: could not create directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata": Permission denied
postgres_1  | initdb: removing contents of data directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata"
```

mike (infra): welcome Tina! this is super common on mac bind mounts. Short checklist: 1) prefer a named docker volume, 2) ensure image arch matches (arm64 on M1), 3) avoid touching DB files from host. If you must initialize a host folder, do chown inside the container.

kelly (eng): +1. We added a helper to the repo to avoid manual host chown because mac bind mounts don't preserve uid/gid as containers expect. Example quick command we use to fix an existing host dir:
```bash
# run a one-off container to chown the mounted path (works for named volumes too by mounting them)
docker compose run --rm --entrypoint sh postgres -c "chown -R 999:999 /var/lib/postgresql/data || true"
# or with docker run on a named volume:
docker run --rm -v redwood_dev_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data --platform linux/arm64 postgres:15 sh -c "chown -R 999:999 /var/lib/postgresql/data"
```
Note: 999 is the postgres uid in official images, but check `id postgres` inside container to be sure.

mike (infra): also consider using `platform: linux/arm64` in compose if Docker pulled an amd64 image under qemu, which can cause subtle permission/behavior differences. Example service snippet from our dev compose:
```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15
    platform: linux/arm64
    volumes:
      - redwood_dev_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: redwood
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: localpass
      POSTGRES_DB: redwood_dev
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
volumes:
  redwood_dev_pgdata:
    driver: local
```

Tina: I tried the chown-in-container trick and platform flag. Postgres starts now but my host `psql` client still can't connect using the socket and our `scripts/db-reset` (which uses host psql/dropdb) errors out.

kelly (eng): we avoid host psql for containerized DB. The tidy pattern is to run db CLIs through the container or a transient helper container that shares network envs. For example:
```bash
# run psql inside the running postgres container
docker compose exec postgres psql -U redwood -d redwood_dev -c "SELECT 1;"
# or use a one-off psql image for scripts
docker run --rm --network $(docker compose network ls -q) -e PGPASSWORD=localpass postgres:15 psql -h postgres -U redwood -d redwood_dev -c "SELECT 1"
```
We added `scripts/psql-in-container` in our repo so CI and devs don't rely on host-level clients.

mike (infra): fwiw, for folks who want native performance: Homebrew postgres is fine — set DATABASE_URL in .env.local and update dev docs. But for parity with CI and to avoid host filesystem shenanigans, containers are recommended.

Tina: thanks — chown inside container + platform flag fixed it for me and I'll switch scripts to use container psql. One odd edge: when using Docker Desktop's osxfs mounts, even after chown-in-container the host shows different perms. Is that expected?

kelly (eng): yep, osxfs translates permissions and ownership to the host user; it's expected. That's another reason to prefer named volumes. If you need fast, reliable bind mounts, some folks use Colima or Mutagen to sync files instead of direct bind mounts.

deploy-bot: Dev docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/dev-setup#postgres-local (internal link) :link:

Tina: great, resolved for my setup — I'll add notes to my onboarding checklist and open a tiny docs PR about Apple Silicon tips. Thanks everyone! :tada:
